info.description:
Welcome to the Desk365 API program!

You can now integrate Desk365 with other applications using the Desk365 API.

If you are interested in using Microsoft Power Automate, Azure Logic Apps or Microsoft Power Apps, please check it out at: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/connectors/desk365/

All the API endpoints require you to pass your API Key in the authorization header.You can try out the API using the web interface below.
  • Click on the Authorize button to enter your API Key.
  • In each API endpoint, click 'Try it out', enter any input parameters if needed and then click 'Execute' to see the results from that endpoint.

For suggestions, questions or to report bugs, contact us at help@desk365.io.

Updates an existing software field identified by name. The field type cannot be changed after creation.

Request and Response objects contain fixed numerical values to indicate Field Type.

  • For "field_type": Text Input=1, Paragraph=2, Checkbox=3, Dropdown=4, Date=5, Number=6, Decimal=7.

Request fields (all optional — only provided fields are updated):

  • 'name': The new field name. It must not exceed 50 characters. System-default fields cannot be renamed.
  • 'is_required': Indicates whether the field is mandatory.
  • 'field_order': An integer greater than or equal to 1 that moves the field to a new position. Values exceeding the total number of fields are capped at the last available position. Moving a field automatically shifts adjacent fields as needed.
  • 'dropdown_choices': An object containing 'add' and/or 'remove' arrays. This field applies only to dropdown fields where type is 4.
    • 'add': An array of new option names to add. Each option must not exceed 50 characters.
    • 'remove': An array of existing option names to remove. Attempting to remove a system-default option returns a 400 error. Providing an option name that does not exist also returns a 400 error.

Query Parameters:

  • field_name (query parameter, required): The name of the software field to update.

Query Parameters:

  • type_name (query parameter, required): The name of the asset type containing the field.
  • field_name (query parameter, required): The current name of the field to update.

Request and Response objects contain fixed numerical values to indicate Field Type.

  • For "type": Text Input=1, Paragraph=2, Checkbox=3, Dropdown=4, Date=5, Number=6, Decimal=7.

Additional notes on field update:

  • All body fields are optional — only the fields provided will be updated.
  • 'name' must not exceed 50 characters if provided. Cannot be set to an empty string.
  • 'is_required' (boolean) — update whether the field is mandatory.
  • 'field_order' (integer, ≥ 1) — move the field to a new position. Values exceeding the total number of fields are capped to the maximum position. Changing the order automatically shifts adjacent fields to accommodate the move.

Dropdown choices (type=4 only):

  • 'dropdown_choices' must be a JSON object (not an array) with optional 'add' and/or 'remove' sub-arrays: {"add": ["Choice A"], "remove": ["Old Choice"]}. This differs from the create endpoint, where 'dropdown_choices' is a flat array of strings.
  • Choices in 'add' must not exceed 50 characters each. New choices are appended after existing ones.
  • Choices in 'remove' are matched by name — unrecognised names are silently ignored.
  • The field must retain at least one dropdown option after removals. Attempting to remove all options returns 400.
  • Passing 'dropdown_choices' for a non-dropdown field is silently ignored.

Protected system-default fields:

  • The following fields cannot be modified in any way (including 'field_order' and 'dropdown_choices') and will return 400: Asset Name, Asset Type, Product (Hardware), Product (Consumable). Any update request targeting these fields is rejected entirely.
  • All other default fields (e.g. Impact, Location) allow updates to 'is_required', 'field_order', and 'dropdown_choices', but do not allow renaming — passing 'name' for them will return 400.
  • Asset State (Hardware) is always required — passing 'is_required' for it will return 400.

post.description:
Appends conversation items (agent replies, contact replies, notes, or forwards) to an existing ticket for migration purposes. No automation or outbound notifications are triggered.

The required query parameter "ticket_number" is the ticket number to append conversations to.

Conversation item fields (each item in the "conversations" array):

  • "type" (required) is one of "reply", "note" or "forward".
  • "sender_type" is "agent" by default or "contact". It is required when the type is set to "reply". A note with sender_type "contact" creates a private contact note (reply to forwarded tickets).
  • "body" (required) is HTML or plain text content. Inline images with public src URLs are re-uploaded automatically; images larger than the helpdesk's inline image size limit are skipped and left as the original URL.
  • "created_on" is the date and time in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format in UTC, and must not be a future date.
  • "created_by" is the email of the agent or contact who authored the item. If omitted or unmatched: reply (agent) defaults to Admin, reply (contact) auto-creates a contact, note (agent) defaults to System, and note (contact) defaults to the ticket contact.
  • "public_note" is true for a public note or false for a private note (note type only; default false). It is ignored when sender_type is "contact" since contact notes are always private.
  • "notified_agents" is a comma-separated list of agent emails to notify (note type only).
  • "cc_address" is a comma-separated list of CC addresses (reply and forward types).
  • "bcc_address" is a comma-separated list of BCC addresses (agent reply and forward types only; not stored for contact replies).
  • "to_address" (required for forward) is the recipient addresses for the forwarded message.
  • "attachment_public_urls" is a comma-separated list of publicly accessible URLs for attachments on this item. The number of URLs is limited to the helpdesk's maximum attachment count, and any excess URLs are skipped with a warning. Each file is virus-scanned before being stored.

A successful response may include a "warnings" array listing non-fatal substitutions, such as an unresolved "created_by" email or skipped "notified_agents" or attachments.

post.description:
Creates one ticket with optional conversations for migration purposes. No automation, round robin, or outbound notifications are triggered. Source is set to Agent Portal.

The only required field is "contact_email". All field names use snake_case.

Ticket field notes:

  • Timestamp fields "created_on", "resolved_on" and "closed_on" use the yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format in UTC and must not be future dates.
  • For "priority": Low=1, Medium=5, High=10, Urgent=20.
  • "group", "assign_to" (agent email), "category", "sub_category", "type", "status" and "form_name" are resolved by name or email. Invalid values return a 400 error.
  • "sub_category" requires "category" to be set.
  • "sla_plan_name" is not specified the contact’s company default SLA plan is used. If the specified plan name is not found, a 400 error is returned.
  • "custom_fields" is a JSON object of custom field values. Keys must use the cf_ prefix, for example cf_employee_id.
  • "watchers" is a comma-separated list of agent emails to add as ticket watchers.
  • "share_to" is a comma-separated list of contact emails to share the ticket with.
  • "attachment_public_urls" is a comma-separated list of publicly accessible URLs. The number of URLs is limited to the helpdesk's maximum attachment count, and any excess URLs are skipped with a warning. Each file is virus-scanned and the combined size must stay within the plan limit.

Conversation item fields (each item in the "conversations" array):

  • "type" (required) is one of "reply", "note" or "forward".
  • "sender_type" is "agent" by default or "contact". It is required when the type is set to "reply". A note with sender_type "contact" creates a private contact note (reply to forwarded tickets).
  • "body" (required) is HTML or plain text content. Inline images with public src URLs are re-uploaded automatically; images larger than the helpdesk's inline image size limit are skipped and left as the original URL.
  • "created_on" is the date and time in yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss format in UTC, and must not be a future date.

  • "public_note" is true for a public note or false for a private note (note type only; default false). It is ignored when sender_type is "contact" since contact notes are always private.
  • "notified_agents" is a comma-separated list of agent emails to notify (note type only).
  • "cc_address" is a comma-separated list of CC addresses (reply and forward types).
  • "bcc_address" is a comma-separated list of BCC addresses (agent reply and forward types only; not stored for contact replies).
  • "to_address" (required for forward) is the recipient addresses for the forwarded message.
  • "attachment_public_urls" is a comma-separated list of publicly accessible URLs for attachments on this item. The number of URLs is limited to the helpdesk's maximum attachment count, and any excess URLs are skipped with a warning. Each file is virus-scanned before being stored.

A successful response may include a "warnings" array listing non-fatal substitutions, such as an unresolved "created_by" email or skipped "notified_agents" or attachments.

Request and Response objects contain fixed numerical values to indicate Priority.

Response object contains fixed numerical value to indicate Source.

  • For "Source": Email=1, Microsoft Teams=5, Support Portal=6, Phone or Other=7, Web Form=12, Web Widget=13, API=15, AI Agent=16.

  • For "updated_by_type" and "closed_by_type": System=1, Agent=2, Contact=3.

Request Object Customization:

  • If you have set up custom ticket fields, use the same name along with the matching case here in "custom_fields" object of the request body to fetch the right results.
  • If you haven't set up any custom ticket fields, remove the "custom_fields" object in the request body and proceed.
  • If you want to use a specific ticket form in the Agent Portal, specify the "form_name" in the object of the request body.
  • If the "form_name" is not specified, the default Agent Portal form will be used to create the ticket.
  • Ticket properties that are not part of the request body will not be changed.

Attachments:

  • Only files on your local machine can be attached using API.
  • The Content-Type of the request should always be 'multipart/form-data'.

Default response is to list all tickets ordered by the created date in descending order without description. There are nine optional fields that can be used while calling this endpoint:
  1. ticket_count - By default you will retrieve 30 tickets per API call. You can customize the count to retrieve 30, 50 or 100 tickets per call.

  2. offset - Paginate through the resulting ticket list using this field.

  3. include_description - By default, description is not included in the response. You can include description in the response using this field.

  4. include_custom_fields - If you use custom ticket fields, you can add them to the response using this field.

  5. include_survey_details - By default, survey ratings are not included in the response. You can include it in the response using this field. 'survey_ratings' is populated only if the survey is sent. If there are multiple ratings for a ticket, the latest survey rating is populated.

  6. nested_fields - If you do not want custom fields and survey details in a nested structure, set this to 1.

  7. order_by - Indicates the sorting criteria.

  8. order_type - ascending or descending.

  9. updated_since - When provided, only tickets that were updated after this time will be returned.

  10. filters - Filter the tickets based on 'status', 'priority', 'type', 'group', 'assigned_to', 'category', 'subcategory', 'source', 'contact', 'company_name' and custom dropdown fields. The 'filters' object should contain an array of string values enclosed in double quotes. Ensure that double quotes, single quotes, and backslashes within the strings are properly escaped with a backslash (\\).

    • Use "--" to indicate an unassigned value for the filter
    • Omit fields from the filter if you prefer not to include them in the filtering process
    • Merged tickets are included by default. Set 'include_merged' in the filters to 0 to exclude merged tickets from the response.

    Sample filters: 

    {
    "status": ["Open", "Pending"],
    "priority": ["1", "10"],
    "type": ["Printer \\'Out of Ink\\' Complaint", "Customer\\'s Request"],
    "group": ["\\"Sales\\" Department", "\\"Marketing\\" Department"],
    "assigned_to": ["user1@example.com", "user2@example.com"],
    "category": ["Hardware", "Software"],
    "subcategory": ["Printer", "Laptop"],
    "source": ["1", "6"],
    "contact": ["customer1@example.com", "customer2@example.com"],
    "company_name": ["Sample Inc", "Contoso Ltd"],
    "custom_fields": {"cf_Country": ["India", "USA"]},
    "include_merged": 0
}

    More information on use of filters can be found here


Response contains fixed numerical values for the below fields:

  • For "Priority": Low=1, Medium=5, High=10, Urgent=20.

  • For first_replied_duration,first_assigned_duration,resolved_duration and closed_duration , the values are represented in minutes.
  • For "updated_by_type" and "closed_by_type": System=1, Agent=2, Contact=3.
  • For "sv_type": Customer Satisfaction = 1, Five Star Rating = 2, Net Promoter Score = 3.
  • For "sv_cs_neutral_type": 'Neither satisfied nor dissatisfied' should be categorized as Positive = 1, Neutral = 2, Negative = 3.
  • For "sv_cs_ratings": Possible values are -3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3. The text mapped to these values can be retrieved from survey details endpoint for the survey type 'Customer Satisfaction' using sv_name.
  • For "conversation_count":Total number of ticket conversations including notes, replies, and forwarded messages.

Query Parameters:

  • offset (query parameter, optional): Pagination offset. Returns next 30 assets starting from this value. Defaults to 0.
  • filterJson (query parameter, optional): JSON string to filter results. Supported keys documented below.
  • sort_by (query parameter, optional): Sort column. Allowed values: created_time, updated_time. Defaults to created_time.
  • sort_order (query parameter, optional): Sort direction. Allowed values: asc, desc. Defaults to desc.

The 'filterJson' parameter accepts a JSON string with the following supported keys:

  • asset_type — Asset type name (string).
  • impact — Array of impact labels. Valid values: Low, Medium, High.
  • end_of_life — Date filter object: {"date": "yyyy-MM-dd", "operator": 0}. Operator: 0=equals, 1=before, 2=after.
  • location — Array of location names.
  • managed_by_group — Array of group names.
  • managed_by_agent — Array of agent email addresses.
  • company — Array of company names.
  • department — Array of department names.
  • used_by — Array of contact email addresses.
  • assigned_on — Date filter object: {"date": "yyyy-MM-dd", "operator": 0}.
  • product — Array of product names.
  • vendor — Array of vendor names.
  • asset_state — Array of asset state names.
  • purchase_date — Date filter object: {"date": "yyyy-MM-dd", "operator": 0}.
  • warranty_expiry_date — Date filter object: {"date": "yyyy-MM-dd", "operator": 0}.
  • depreciation — Array of depreciation names.
  • last_audit_date — Date filter object: {"date": "yyyy-MM-dd", "operator": 0}.
  • search_term — Search by asset name (string, max 256 characters).

Any unrecognised key returns a 400 validation error. Invalid filter values (e.g. non-existent location names, unknown agent emails) also return a 400 validation error.

    "assigned_on": { "date": "2025-01-01", "operator": 0 },

    "asset_state": ["In Use"],

    "depreciation": ["5-Year Straight Line"],
